axes.model_access:
**It uses the CLI's agent and configuration; the model is switchable.**

**Official IDE page wording**: "It uses the same agent as the Codex CLI and shares the same configuration"

Models listed on the official pricing page:

- GPT-5.5
- GPT-5.4
- GPT-5.4 mini
- Pro additionally has GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark (research preview)

Below the chat input there is a **model switcher**, with reasoning effort adjustable (`low` / `medium` / `high`).

**The default model is set in the shared `config.toml`** (`model = "..."`), shared by IDE and CLI,
so custom providers go through the same `model_providers` configuration (see the CLI / SDK dossiers).

**BYOK works**: the official supports logging in with an API key; the JetBrains integration can also ride a JetBrains AI subscription.
On the API-key path, the usable model range follows that key's API models.
axes.runtime:
**It is an extension, not a standalone editor.**

**Official README wording**: "If you want Codex in your code editor (VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf), install in your IDE."

That is: **install into an existing editor such as VS Code / Cursor / Windsurf**.

This is a different form from Zed (standalone editor) and Cline Desktop (native app).
axes.local_files:
Accesses workspace files through the host editor.

Context comes from open files, selections and `@file` references.
There is also **Auto Context**: automatically pulling in recent files and IDE context
(see `/auto-context`).

Official stance: workspace = current directory plus temp directories (e.g. `/tmp`); writes default to the workspace.

On Windows it can run natively (via the Windows sandbox) or switch to WSL2
(setting `chatgpt.runCodexInWindowsSubsystemForLinux`).

**The official IDE docs describe no standalone semantic index** —
local file retrieval is done by the same agent's tools.

**Verification**: checked the official features and settings pages.
axes.background:
**There is a cloud form: the official says tasks can be delegated from the IDE to Codex Cloud.**

**IDE page wording**: "delegate tasks to Codex Cloud"

**Features page wording**: "Offload longer jobs to a cloud environment"

Switch with `/cloud` and `/local`.

Cloud tasks run in the background (including in parallel) inside **OpenAI-managed containers**,
so **cloud tasks keep going after the local editor is closed**.
**Local tasks depend on the host editor process — close it and they stop.**

Cloud tasks and local messages share plan usage (the official pricing page says a shared 5-hour window).
axes.tools:
**Built-in first-party tools and commands are all verified.**

Tools:

- web search — the official says enabled by default, via an OpenAI-maintained search cache, configurable `web_search = "live" | "disabled"`
- image generation — `$imagegen`, model `gpt-image-2`, counts against usage and drains quota faster
- code review — `/review`
- editor context — `@file`, selections, drag-in images

Command-palette commands: `chatgpt.newChat` / `addToThread` / `addFileToThread` / `implementTodo`,
plus TODO CodeLens.

**MCP is explicitly supported in the IDE extension officially.**

STDIO and Streamable HTTP supported; CLI and IDE share
`[mcp_servers.<name>]` in `config.toml` (including `enabled_tools`, and per-server, per-tool `approval_mode`).

**Original wording**: "Codex supports MCP servers in both the CLI and the IDE extension"
axes.context:
**The app-server architecture remains the key design** — threads can be started, resumed and recovered;
IDE and CLI share the same session mechanics and the same configuration.

The official adds three more points:

- launching a cloud task from a local session remembers the session context (and context is kept when a cloud task returns to local to continue)
- `/status` shows the thread ID, context usage and rate limits
- `/goal` can set a persistent goal

**Concrete context-window numbers and the automatic compaction policy are not given separately in the IDE docs.**

Compaction on the CLI / SDK side goes through config keys such as `compact_prompt`;

**Verification**: checked the official features and slash-commands pages.
axes.permissions:
**IDE and CLI share the same sandbox and approvals.**

**Official settings page wording**: "The Codex IDE extension uses the Codex CLI"

**Same page**: approvals and sandbox are configured in the shared `~/.codex/config.toml`.

The UI side has three approval modes: `Chat` / `Agent` / `Agent (Full Access)`.

- default `Agent` — reads/writes and executes commands automatically inside the working directory, **but outside the working directory or for networking it still asks**
- only `Full Access` skips approval for networking

Official security page stance (covering the IDE extension):
by default **no network + writes limited to the current workspace**; `.git` / `.agents` / `.codex` recursively read-only.

Approval and sandbox keys are the same as the CLI: `approval_policy` / `sandbox_mode` /
`[sandbox_workspace_write] network_access` and the `network_proxy` domain list.
The Windows native sandbox defaults to `elevated`.
axes.fit:
Fits two kinds of people:

- those already using VS Code / Cursor / Windsurf-style editors who want Codex in the same environment without switching tools
- those who need IDE and CLI to share sessions (the app-server architecture)

sections.形态澄清（这一条最容易被误解）:
It explicitly lists three supported host editors.

> Official README wording: "If you want Codex in your code editor (VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf), install in your IDE."

**Key information**: this shows the **Codex IDE form is an "extension", not an "editor"**.

### Comparing the three IDE-class forms

| Form | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **Standalone editor** | Zed | ships a full editor; AI is part of it |
| **Native desktop app** | Cline Desktop | attaches to no editor |
| **Editor extension** | **Codex IDE**, Copilot, the Cline extension | installs into an existing editor |

**This distinction matters**:

- in the extension form, "indexing strategy" and "context building" are often decided by the host editor, not by this tool itself
- so this entry is not fully comparable with [Zed](./zed.md) — one is a standalone editor, the other an extension
sections.与 CLI 形态的关系:
Two entries, different categories, but a shared backend:

| | [CLI form](../../coding/products/codex-cli.md) | IDE form (this entry) |
|---|---|---|
| Form | terminal process | editor extension |
| Authorization | rides the ChatGPT subscription | **the same authorization** |
| Backend | app server | **the same app server** |

**The practical meaning of the app-server architecture**: threads can be started, resumed and recovered.

So **a session opened in the IDE can be continued in the CLI**, and vice versa.

**This is the tool's most valuable architectural feature**, and the reason the CLI and IDE entries must cross-reference each other.
